newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Communists threaten Yeltsin with impeachment.
newsitem.headline: Communists threaten Yeltsin with impeachment.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin's communist opponents in parliament said on Monday they may try to impeach him over his order to withdraw all Russian troops from Chechnya and over Moscow's accord with the region's separatists.

The communist chairman of the State Duma's security committee told reporters an emergency debate called for Friday should discuss impeachment and a vote of no confidence in the government. Impeachment moves, which have failed against Yeltsin before, have almost no chance of success under the constitution.

"The deputies are not going to limit themselves to generating hot air," Viktor Ilyukhin said of next Friday's debate. "I think the questions of impeachment and of confidence in the government will be raised."

The debate was called on Sunday on a communist initiative after Yeltsin ordered the troops out and Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin signed a framework agreement on Saturday with Chechen government leader Aslan Maskhadov. The deal gives the region considerable autonomy ahead of elections on January 27.

Duma speaker Gennady Seleznyov, another communist, said he could not rule out an impeachment move if it appeared that Yeltsin's action had breached the constitution. The communists say Yeltsin's action will lead to the break-up of Russia.

Impeachment requires two-thirds majorities in both chambers of parliament and the approval of both the Supreme Court and Constitutional Court -- all within a time limit of three months. There is little chance of that. The Duma also has little power to oust the government against Yeltsin's wishes.
